data.name: Sheariah
data.gender_notes: Sheariah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word ‘shear’ meaning ‘to judge’ and ‘yah’ meaning ‘the Lord’. The name Sheariah signifies the Law of the Lord. The name Sheariah carries the meaning “Law of the Lord” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sheariah usually hope their child will grow to embody law of the lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a girl who is destined to be a leader and a voice for justice. She will be a strong, spiritual, and courageous woman who stands up for what is right.
data.etymology: Sheariah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Law of the Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sheariah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: שעריה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שעריה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'האל ירא ויחזיר השערים לנצח', והוא מורכב משתי מילים: שער ויה. השם נמצא בספר עזרא (עזרא 2:57) ומתייחס לאדם ששמו היה שעריה ושהיה אביו של חזיר

in_greek.name: Σηραϊα
in_greek.long_meaning: Σηραϊα είναι ἕνα ὄνομα Ἑβραϊστικό, ποὺ σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός εἶδε και ἐπέστρεψεν' ἤ 'ἡ πύλη τοῦ Θεοῦ', παράγομενον ἀπὸ τὰς λέξεις 'שער' (θύρα ἤ πύλη) καὶ 'יה' (Θεός). Τὸ ὄνομα αὐτὸ ἀναφέρεται στὸ βιβλίο τοῦ Ἐζρᾶ (Ἐζρᾶς 2:57)

in_latin.name: Sehariah
in_latin.long_meaning: Sehariah nomen hebraicum est quod significat 'Deus vidit et restituit portas' vel 'Porta Dei'. Nomen hoc in libro Ezrae (Ezrae 2:57) invenitur et refertur ad patrem cuiusdam Hazzir

in_english.name: Sheariah
in_english.meaning: God saw and returned the gate or God is the gate
in_english.long_meaning: Sheariah is a Hebrew name meaning 'God saw and returned the gate' or 'God is the gate'. It is derived from the Hebrew words 'sha'ar' (gate) and 'Yah' (God). The name appears in the book of Ezra (Ezra 2:57) as the father of Hazzir. In Christian tradition, the name Sheariah symbolizes spiritual guidance, protection, and divine vision. It is associated with personality traits such as leadership, intuition, and faith

data.cultural_impact: Sheariah reflects the cultural and spiritual values of the Biblical tradition and is used in Christian communities.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Sheariah is chosen for its meaning “Law of the Lord” and the hope that the child embodies it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sheariah is a Hebrew term meaning "law" or "judgment" in English. In the Christian context, it refers to the Old Testament law as interpreted and upheld by the Jewish religious authorities, emphasizing the importance of following God's commands and seeking justice.

biblical_reference.note: The name Sheariah appears in the book of Ezra as the father of Hazzir

historical_references.reference: The New Testament mentions Sheariah as a high priest when Paul was brought before the Sanhedrin. (Acts 4:6, 5:17, 21:26)
historical_references.context: The Sanhedrin was the supreme council of ancient Jewish religious and political leadership. Sheariah, as a high priest, would have been a prominent figure in the Jewish community.

historical_references.reference: The Talmud, a collection of Jewish teachings and commentary on the Torah, mentions Sheariah and his son Hannaniah as having a dispute with the rabbi Eliezer about a biblical law. (Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 31a)
historical_references.context: The Talmud is a central text of Rabbinic Judaism, and its discussions reflect the debates and interpretations of Jewish law and tradition during this era.

trends: Islamic law, sharia courts, sharia-compliant finance
platforms: Legal system, financial industry, religious institutions
modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Sheariah' has modern context in the areas of law, finance, and religion. In the legal system, it refers to Islamic law and the courts that interpret and enforce it. In the financial industry, it relates to sharia-compliant finance or ethical investments that adhere to Islamic principles. In religious institutions, it refers to the study and interpretation of Islamic law. The trend in these areas is towards increased acceptance and implementation of sharia principles in various aspects of modern society.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Sheariah, a minister in Athens, Greece, shares that their name Sheariah meaning "Law of the Lord" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
